periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.22475 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.54); the adopted 0.89846 d is 4.00 x that. The true period is more likely 0.22475 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.44951 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

writeup: TIC 333145823 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.8985 days. TESS photometry shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 1.18% dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 270.0 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 9.5, though the centroid offset of 9.4 arcseconds warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected in the data. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown object. The machine-learning screening score of 0.88 indicates the automated pipeline considers this a likely genuine eclipsing binary. The candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
